From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French gangue. Doublet of gang.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • enPR: găng, IPA(key): /ɡæŋ/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -æŋ
  • Homophone: gang

Noun

[edit]

gangue (countable and uncountable, plural gangues)

  1. (mining) The earthy waste substances occurring in metallic ore.
    Coordinate term: country
    • 1995, Paul T. Craddock, Early Metal Mining and Production, page 147:
      Thus the percentage recovery of metal from the ore was much higher than in the primitive process where the semi-vitrified gangue and half-smelted ore are typically rich in prills of copper and copper minerals.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • veinstone

Derived terms

[edit]
  • endogangue
  • exogangue

Translations

[edit]
earthy waste substances occurring in metallic ore
  • Arabic: غَثّ m (ḡaṯṯ), شَوْب m (šawb), شَوَائِبُ الرِّكَاز m (šawāʔibu r-rikāz)
  • Chinese:
    Cantonese: 脈石 / 脉石 (mak6 sek6)
    Mandarin: 脈石 / 脉石 (zh) (màishí)
  • Esperanto: gango
  • Finnish: sivukivi (fi)
  • French: gangue (fr) f
  • German: Gang (de) m, Gangart (de) f, Gangerz n
  • Italian: ganga (it) f
  • Japanese: 脈石 (ja) (みゃくせき, myakuseki)
  • Korean: 맥석 (ko) (maekseok)
  • Portuguese: ganga (pt) f
  • Russian: пуста́я поро́да f (pustája poróda)
  • Spanish: ganga (es) f, blancarte m

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

A borrowing from German Gang (“way, path, trail, track, course, line, duct”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɡɑ̃ɡ/
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

gangue f (plural gangues)

  1. (geology, mining) gangue

Further reading

[edit]
  • “gangue”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Portuguese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • gang (dated)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from English gang.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈɡɐ̃.ɡi/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈɡɐ̃.ɡi/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈɡɐ̃.ɡe/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈɡɐ̃.ɡɨ/

  • Hyphenation: gan‧gue

Noun

[edit]

gangue (Portugal) m or (Brazil) f (plural gangues)

  1. gang; street gang (criminal group, especially one that practices petty crime)
    Synonyms: quadrilha, bando, (well organised) facção
  2. gang (a group of friends who do things together regularly, especially mischievous children)
    Synonyms: turma, patota

Derived terms

[edit]
  • ganguezinha (diminutive) (Brazil)

Related terms

[edit]
  • gângster

Further reading

[edit]
  • “gangue”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “gangue”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
